status_corrections.actual_source_outcome: The Definition allows empty input/output index sets and any finite receptive-field K. If K is empty its sum is zero and y(p)=b; if O is empty the output is the unique empty function. Channel counts and stride coordinates remain positive.
With every filter matrix W_delta and bias b zero, the displayed finite sum is zero at each output site for any boundary extension; this is an admitted zero-output layer.
For one input and output channel and a singleton receptive field K={delta}, the formula reduces to y(p)=b+xtilde(a+s* p+delta)W_delta, a single scalar weighted input plus bias.

A receptive field with no offsets gives the spatially constant bias output, while an empty output set has no sites to evaluate. Neither case needs a nonexistent maximum or division in the convolution formula.

If X is empty, a supplied layer Phi:X->Y is the unique empty function and the displayed equivariance identity is vacuous. If Y is empty and X is nonempty no such supplied function exists; that pair is outside the layer data.

For the one-element group the only action element is the identity, so equivariance reduces to Phi(x)=Phi(x) and every supplied function is equivariant. This follows directly from the displayed action identity.

A trivial output action is explicitly admitted: Tprime_g is the identity for every g, and the Definition names the resulting equivariant condition G-invariance. Input and output actions are not required to coincide.
By the defining criterion, a layer called G-equivariant satisfies Phi(T_g x)=Tprime_g Phi(x) for every g and x. This is the forward reading of its stated property definition.

Conversely, a supplied layer satisfying the displayed identity for all group elements and inputs meets exactly the Definition of G-equivariance; no equality of the input and output actions is additionally required.

A filter with empty support is the zero filter and both displayed correlations are zero; the corresponding sums converge absolutely. The group itself cannot be empty because it contains its identity, and channel counts stay positive.
If f or Psi is identically zero, each matrix-product summand vanishes, so the output correlation is zero at every g. This meets the stated finite-support/absolute-convergence requirement.

For a one-element group G={e}, the group-to-group correlation has the single term f(e)Psi(e). With one input and output channel it is ordinary scalar multiplication; the lattice-to-group formula retains its own lattice index set.

No invertibility or full-rank condition is imposed on the filter matrices. Zero or singular channel-mixing matrices are admitted and their products are still defined, subject only to the explicit support/convergence condition.
